messages:
elaine-sec: Heads up — vuln-scan flagged a libssh heap overflow (CVE-2026-9999) in our base image debian-slim-2025-11. Scanner: clair/registry-hook. Impact: potential container escape when components load libssh. I think we should kick an emergency base-image rebuild, sign with KMS, and do a staged canary. @devon-sre @sam-ops

devon-sre: ack. can you paste the scanner output and which layers are affected?

elaine-sec: sure, see excerpt from the report:
```
Component: libssh 0.9.6
Vuln: CVE-2026-9999
Vector: heap-based overflow in ssh_transport.c
Layers: /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libssh.so.4 (layer sha256:abc123)
Confidence: HIGH
Exploitability: LOW-MED (requires crafted input to server component)
Recommendation: rebuild base image with libssh upgrade to 0.10.x or use musl-based minimal image where libssh not present
```

sam-ops: KMS/signing notes — our current flow: cosign uses the KMS signing key projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/images/cryptoKeys/cosign-key. If we rotate the image we need to ensure the signer principal has access and that the registry's signature verification policy is updated if we change signer identity.

cosign-bot: Reminder: existing signed images will still verify until key is revoked. New signed images must be pushed to staging registry first.

anne-sec: RBAC point: the image-rebuilder service account will need putObject/write to staging registry and attestor role for signing. Suggest policy: grant storage.objects.create + storage.objects.get on gs://redwood-staging-images and iam.serviceAccounts.actAs for cosign runner only. Keep perms minimal.

devon-sre: operational ask: what's the blast radius? Which clusters use this base image? We need a targeted rollout list.

elaine-sec: quick lookup: prod (model-serving, batch-infer), staging, test, and a handful of internal dev clusters. I'll attach a list in the PR but short-term: block new deployments using debian-slim-2025-11, allow existing running pods to continue for 24h while we canary.

beth-plat: audit logging: please ensure we emit an image-rebuild.trace_id and the KMS key version used to our logging pipeline. Add fields: rebuild.initiator, rebuild.reason, rebuild.commit, signing.key_version. Route to Splunk index image_rebuilds and retention 90d.

elaine-sec: agreed. We'll add a logship sidecar step in the rebuild pipeline. Also will tag artifacts with SLSA provenance where possible.

sam-ops: cosign command I'm going to use for staging sign (example):
```bash
COSIGN_EXPERIMENTAL=1 cosign sign --kms projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/images/cryptoKeys/cosign-key --annotations rebuild.reason="CVE-2026-9999" gcr.io/redwood-staging/base:debian-slim-2025-11-fix1
```
Make sure the KMS key has a binding for svc-account:ci-cosign@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com

anne-sec: for the RBAC change in registry, we should open a short-lived PR to infra-iam with the minimal bindings and an expiry (2 weeks) so the canary tooling can push. Then roll back extra perms.

devon-sre: canary plan suggestion: 1) push rebuilt image to staging; 2) smoke run on staging infra; 3) Canary to prod-model-serving at 5% traffic for 30m; 4) if no regressions, 20% for 1h; 5) full cutover. Keep auto-rollback if error rate > 1% or latency 2x baseline.

elaine-sec: add vuln-specific test: run fuzz harness against ssh parsing path in container to validate fix before canary accepts traffic. Also run runtime sec checks (seccomp, no-new-privs verification).

beth-plat: tie alerts to incident channel: incidents -> subscribe to rebuild.traces. Also snapshot audit logs before PR merge in case we need forensics.

devon-sre: timeline? I can schedule the rebuild in the 2-hour maintenance window tonight if sec sign-off by EOD.

elaine-sec: I can sign off once the fuzz run finishes (~3h). I'll update the PR with results.

sam-ops: operational checklist (short):
- build image (upgrade libssh)
- run unit + fuzz tests
- run container-scan (clair/snyk)
- sign with cosign KMS key (cosign-bot to verify)
- push to staging, run smoke
- trigger canary release per devon's plan
- rotate key if compromise suspected (not necessary now)

devon-sre: add runbook pointer when we open the PR: /runbooks/image-rebuild-canary.md (small edits to include new checks).

elaine-sec: opening PR now: https://git.redwood.internal/platform/image-rebuilds/pulls/221 - includes CI job, RBAC PR template, audit mapping, and canary policy.

deploy-bot: Scheduled "image-rebuild-base-libssh-fix" for 2026-03-18T02:00:00Z (maintenance window).

anne-sec: one last note — ensure attestation metadata includes the exact KMS key version. If we later need to revoke a key, having the version in logs is critical for forensics.

elaine-sec: noted. I'll add signing.key_version + cosign.digest to the audit payload. I'll also post results here when the fuzz suite completes. :white_check_mark:
